name: addERI_Proxmox_VE
description: Sets an ERI on a Proxmox VE node's resource so Proxmox_VE_Topology can attach its node vertex to it.
technicalNotes:
OPTIONAL, and off by default. Applies only to a resource carrying pve.topology.enabled=true (lowercase). Proxmox_VE_Topology and addERI_Proxmox_VE share that one property and are only useful together: the map needs the node ERI this PropertySource stamps, and the ERI exists only for the map. Turn it on where the guests are also monitored as their own resources; otherwise the map has nothing to draw them as.

Stamps one ERI key, in its own category "proxmoxve" so it combines with the MAC-based ERIs a monitored Linux resource already carries rather than replacing them -- LogicMonitor keeps the highest priority within a category and merges across categories.

The key is synthesised from the cluster and node names because Proxmox exposes no hardware identifier for a node anywhere in its API: /cluster/status gives name, ip and nodeid, /nodes/{node}/status gives none, and /nodes/{node}/network has no hwaddr. VMware does not need this because vCenter hands out each ESXi host's hardware UUID. pveTopoKey in the preamble is the single definition of the key's shape, and Proxmox_VE_Topology calls the same helper -- the two must produce byte-identical keys or every node vertex silently stops matching its resource.

The node it stamps is the one the resource is, not any node in the cluster: /cluster/status marks the responding node with local=true. Without that, every node would be stamped with the same key.

Silent on any failure, like addCategory_Proxmox_VE: it runs against resources that may not be Proxmox, and a PropertySource that prints on a host it does not understand corrupts that resource's properties.
